thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager triggered: high 5xx rate on /v1/generate (hosted-prod). Alert threshold breached at 1864443210

pagerduty-bot: Paging oncall: @Priya S — escalation level 1. See runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/runbooks/api-errors

Alex K: Seeing this in the metric dashboard — 5xx spike at 23:07 UTC. Latency also climbed for some p95 requests.

Priya S: On it. I’m pulling the prod logs now. Any customer-facing pages?

Maria L: Support has 3 tickets open mentioning truncated responses and timeouts, one is an enterprise customer (acme-corp). Notified CSM.

Samir D: I can help with logs + traces. Quick check — are we sampling traces more aggressively since the redeploy?

Alex K: We rolled a small release to routing rules ~20m before the spike. Not sure if related.

Priya S: Repro steps: curling generate with a simple prompt returns 502 for some requests. Intermittent.

Priya S: Running an ad-hoc query against logs: ```
# query: last 15m
service:hosted-api status:5.. status!=429 | count()
```

Priya S: Hm logs show a lot of downstream "backend-unavailable" errors from our model-proxy pool. But traces are sparse.

Jing W: I’m not seeing corresponding traces for many of these requests — sampling rate at 1% for prod, that might be hiding the root. Increasing trace sampling now to 20% for the route.

Samir D: Copy. Also, I suspect trace IDs aren't being propagated from the edge -> model-proxy for requests hitting certain nodes. If so, logs will look orphaned.

Alex K: Good call. Anyone have a quick grep to confirm missing trace headers on proxy logs?

Priya S: Running: ```
# check for trace header presence
grep -E "trace_id=|X-Request-ID" /var/log/hosted-api/proxy/*.log | head
```

Priya S: Output shows many entries without trace_id. A subset have `trace_id=null`.

Maria L: That explains the sparse traces. If trace IDs are not propagated, our distributed span correlation fails.

Priya S: Timeline so far: 23:00 deploy of routing change, 23:07 spikes begin, 23:10 alerts fire, 23:11 oncall paged, 23:14 increased trace sampling, 23:18 first partial mitigation (drain two model-proxy nodes)

Samir D: Hypothesis A: routing change introduced a misconfiguration that disables trace header forwarding on a subset of proxies -> causes model-proxy to treat requests as new sessions and overwhelm backend (connection churn), leading to 5xx.

Samir D: Hypothesis B: a mis-quantized model variant was rolled to a subset -> memory thrash -> backend errors. Need model-serving logs to confirm.

Priya S: Can someone fetch model-proxy logs for the nodes we drained? I want to see pod-level errors and connection resets.

Alex K: Pasting pod error snippet: ```
[23:06:58] proxy-node-17 ERROR connection reset by peer while forwarding to model-backend
[23:07:02] proxy-node-17 WARN failed to acquire session: timeout
[23:07:03] proxy-node-21 ERROR missing trace header, creating synthetic id
```

Jing W: That "missing trace header" line is interesting — shows we create synthetic ids rather than propagate. That would break correlation. Did the routing change introduce a sidecar config override?

Priya S: I’m looking at the canary routing diff: https://git.redwood.ai/routing/changes/merge/2043 — it toggles `preserve_headers=false` for the new rule. Oops.

Alex K: That seems likely causal. Removing header preservation would strip trace headers for requests routed that path.

Samir D: If that's true, mitigation = revert the routing rule or create override to preserve headers. We should revert the change in the next 5-10 minutes while we validate.

Priya S: Rolling a rollback to routing rule now. Applying patch: ```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: routing-config
data:
  preserve_headers: "true"
EOF
```

Maria L: Heads up to support: telling ACME they're seeing degraded responses, mitigation in progress.

incident-bot: Deploy started by Priya S — routing-config rollback (change id 2043-revert) at 1864443450

Priya S: After rollback, I see a drop in 5xx counts on the summary graph within ~30s for the subset of traffic that went through the affected path. Not fully back to baseline yet.

Alex K: Can we verify trace propagation returned? Checking proxy logs for `trace_id=` now.

Priya S: New log samples show trace headers present again. Example: ```
[23:19:12] proxy-node-17 INFO forwarded request trace_id=abcd-1234
```

Jing W: I can now see more spans in the traces — requests correlate through edge->proxy->model-backend. Some of the earlier 5xx were due to backend overload from connection churn.

Samir D: Good. Still want to confirm model-serving health — fetching model logs for the timeframe 23:06-23:12.

Priya S: Model-serving logs show increased session creation and a handful of OOM-ish messages (GC/alloc pressure) on a specific GPU pool. Those map to the same nodes that had missing trace headers. Could be simultaneous but root cause seems routing header drop.

Maria L: Customer impact: ACME reported partial failures 23:07-23:22; support updated them at 23:20 with mitigation steps. No data exfiltration or PII impact. Logged in incident ticket INC-2026-042.

Samir D: Next steps while monitoring: 1) Revert routing change permanently for now 2) Add unit test to routing CI to ensure headers preserved 3) Increase trace sampling for 1h to capture additional correlation 4) Run ad-hoc query to rebuild timeline with now-available traces

Alex K: On timeline building — I’m exporting request ids and matching across logs/traces. Query used: ```
# export request ids where status=5xx and duration>3000ms
service:hosted-api status:5* | json field=request_id | uniq()
```

Priya S: Sharing a short timeline CSV paste (request_id,timestamp,node,status): ```
req-01,23:06:58,proxy-17,502
req-02,23:07:01,proxy-21,502
req-03,23:07:05,proxy-17,502
```

Jing W: Observability gap notes (to include in RCA): - Trace sampling low by default, which delayed correlation - Routing config change lacked an automated test for header propagation - Some logs had `trace_id=null` which made ad-hoc queries incomplete - Dashboard alerting threshold triggered before we had correlated traces

Maria L: Also note: log retention settings truncated some debug logs after 7 days; if this persists we should extend retention for proxy logs for 30 days for postmortems.

Priya S: Marking current severity as reduced. Continuing to monitor for 20m. If stable, we’ll close paging and start formal post-incident RCA doc.

Alex K: Quick patch for CI: add test that runs a routing simulate and asserts X-Trace-ID is forwarded. Will open PR after this.

Samir D: For the RCA document — I’ll own the hypothesis writeup. Jing can own observability action items. Maria can handle customer communications and timeline.

Priya S: Thanks all — great rapid collaboration. If anyone sees another spike ping this thread.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity -> mitigated at 1864443810

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by @Priya S at 1864443812

Alex K: Final note — add check in the rollouts runbook to verify `preserve_headers` when changing routing rules.

Maria L: Adding that to the postmortem checklist and kicking off the RCA doc INC-2026-042/rca. Link will be posted here when ready. :white_check_mark:
